name: PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Alamtri Resources Indonesia: parts marked, discount persistent, one mark to test
frontmatter.summary: Alamtri trades below the marked value of its parts. The September accounts show the smelter's first aluminium sales and a profit step, but a debt-funded distribution turned net cash into net debt. We mark the listed stake at its price, the contractor at interim net assets and the parent's securities at fair value, hold a 30% discount and rate HOLD at Rp2,118; the dated buyback window does not close it.
thesis: The parts are worth Rp2,108 a share after a 30% holding-company discount; the tape at Rp2,310 implies a discount of 23% to that net asset value, so the market is paying the subsidiary's price and very little for the contractor, the joint ventures, the securities book and the parent's net cash [S18, S0, F44].

The discount is the base rate, not the thesis: the one dated capital action is the buyback approved at the 17 April 2026 AGMS, up to 5.0 trillion rupiah over 12.0 months from 18 April 2026 with execution from 20 October 2026, but a discretionary repurchase of less than a tenth of the shares does not crystallise the unlisted parts, so we hold the discount at the middle of the house band rather than assume it closes [S20, S21, S13].

The September print is an operating step, not a valuation step: nine-month revenue of US$1,901.5m already exceeds FY2025, aluminium sales of US$522.4m are the new line, and parent profit was US$516.6m; the distribution of US$447.5m exceeded operating cash flow of US$390.7m and was funded with new bank loans [S18].

The P/BV cross-check now carries no weight: its own-history average straddles the AADI separation, and its FY2022A observation is struck on the pre-separation entity, so it is not comparable with the September 2026 parent-attributable book of US$5,031.4m it would be applied to; at the post-separation-only average the leg prints below the add threshold, so the rating is a hold on either reading [S0, S18, F57].

The bull and bear move the discount only, because the engine's scenario layer cannot shock a static market mark; the securities and joint-venture marks are fair value rather than floors, and we size that exposure here rather than in the scenario column [S18, F52, F53].

catalysts.event: End of the buyback window approved at the 17 April 2026 AGMS, a ceiling set at the AGMS for twelve months from 18 April 2026, execution begun on 20 October 2026
Full application of the state export channel, when coal may be exported only through PT DSI under PP No. 24/2026 and Permendag No. 15/2026
Full-year results and the size of the following distribution against the near-total payout
Annual general meeting, where the FY2026 distribution and any capital action are decided
Decision point on the North Kalimantan hydropower build and the industrial park funding

blocks.text: This revision changes the rating, and the reason is a mechanic, not the story. The audit was right that the P/BV cross-check decided the call on a multiple that is not perimeter-consistent: its own-history average spans four fiscal years that straddle the AADI separation [S0, S13]. We have re-weighted to the parts alone: the total return falls to **3.3%** including the forward distribution of **Rp269**, the target is **Rp2,118** and the rating is **HOLD** [S18, S0]. The corrections that stand: cash is the filing's cash and cash equivalents, not the pack's wider line that folds current investments in [S13, F72, F73]; the parent's US$105.0m FVTPL sleeve is a valued part [S18, F74, F75]; and the contractor mark is cited to the interim segment note [S18, F63, F64].

Marked on the parts, the stake in the listed subsidiary is at its own traded price, the contractor at its September segment net assets, the joint ventures at book, the parent's securities at fair value and the parent's own cost base capitalised and deducted [S13, S18, F33, F44, F52, F53, F63, F74]. That gives an SOTP of **Rp2,108**, and it is now the whole of the blend at **Rp2,108** [S0]. The tape applies a discount of **23%** to the SOTP net asset value and we underwrite **30%**, the middle of the house band; the one dated capital action, the buyback window to April 2027, is priced below that net asset value per share but is too small to close a discount of this width [S13, S20, S21].

We did not delete the leg because it lifted the answer: on the post-separation observations alone the book multiple is lower but above the primary, and weighting it would put the target a little higher, still inside the hold range, so both readings agree on the call [S0, S18]. What would change the call is disclosed buyback execution, a re-rating of the listed subsidiary toward its house value, or a distribution step-up the cash flow can carry [S6, S13, S14, S20].

The first mark to test is the subsidiary, more than half of the gross parts, because the house's own coverage of it is a reduce, well below its traded price [S0, F33]. We keep the market mark — the executable value of a listed minority stake and the card's default — but publish the alternate: re-marking the stake to the house value lowers the blend to just above the bear column's **Rp1,777** and takes the total return to about minus eight per cent once the Rp269 distribution is counted, a stronger sell case than a hold [S0, F33]. The call is therefore a hold on the traded marks, not a bet on the subsidiary's price.

The variant view is narrow: the market pays the subsidiary's tape plus a fraction of the rest, and does not believe the unlisted carrying values [S13, S0]. We differ only in the discount we will underwrite, and the middle of the house band does not pay for a position: the discount is the base rate, and the buyback window does not by itself crystallise it.

Indonesian holding companies in the middle of a downstreaming transition look expensive on earnings or
cheap on assets depending on where the cycle is standing, and the honest way to value one is part by
part rather than through a consolidated cash flow. The weakness is always the same: the parts that are
easy to mark flatter the answer, and the hard ones are where the argument is.

Alamtri is the listed parent of a metallurgical-coal and aluminium group. It owns **85%** of PT Alamtri Minerals Indonesia (ADMR), the listed vehicle that holds the met-coal concessions and the aluminium smelter; all of the mining services contractor; a portfolio of power, transmission and hydro joint ventures carried at **US$740.2m**; a securities book; and parent net cash [S13, S18, F33, F52]. The September segment note shows the change in the mix: of **US$1,901.5m** of nine-month revenue, **US$522.4m** was aluminium sold to third parties, a line that did not exist a year earlier, and the rest was the coal and services books [S18, F46, F61].

The strategy is downstreaming: convert a price-taking export coal business into a contracted domestic industrial one by smelting aluminium in North Kalimantan on the group's hydro joint ventures [S7, S14]. The smelter is ramping through nameplate capacity, which is why the segment note now carries metal revenue and the capex guide fell from the construction peak [S14, F37, F38, F39]. The coal concessions remain the cash engine, the contractor is largely an internal service provider, and the power and hydro ventures are strategic inputs [S7, S13]. The coal tenure is contractual: five coal contracts of work held through the subsidiary's AMC entities, each with a thirty-year operating period from first mining, so the licence is a contract of work rather than an IUPK [S13, S14].

Scale is modest and integration is the position. Metallurgical sales volume was **6.28** million tonnes in the last reported year at an actual strip ratio of **3.55** [S3]. The group owns the hauling, barging and logistics chain, which lowers the cost of getting tonnes to a buyer without stopping another producer selling to the same buyer; the moat is narrow: integration, a branded metallurgical slate and a captive industrial park [S7].

Ownership is concentrated: the data pack's insider field is **69.0%** and its free float **26.6%**, which do not exhaust the register, so we read the residual as treasury and other non-float holdings rather than a complete cap table [S0, S8]. The controlling shareholder is the founding family's vehicle, and the listed subsidiary is separately traded, so minority holders own a look-through position in both [S13, S7].

The group sits between two commodity markets and the house decks price both. The coal deck prints **US$150/t** a tonne, above its current-year forecast of **US$137/t** and well above its long-run marker of **US$105/t**; the aluminium deck prints **US$3,179/t** with a long-run marker of **US$3,000/t**, and we adopt both reversion paths in full as the reviewed house view [S0]. Neither is the price this group realises — the coal is metallurgical and the aluminium is not yet sold at a benchmark — so both enter as context for the parts, not as the driver of one consolidated cash flow [S7, S0].

Regulation is the second structural force. The royalty regime keys contract-continuation licences to a step schedule on the reference coal price, so a higher reference means a higher rate rather than proportionally higher proceeds; the audited charge for this group was **US$124.6m** on the coal book in FY2025, well below the headline band because the levy is on the reference, not the realised price [S12, S13, F17].

The export channel is the dated change. Under PP No. 24/2026 and Permendag No. 15/2026, coal may be exported only through the state exporter PT Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia from 1 January 2027, and registered exporter permits lapse at the end of 2026 [S15, S16]. The producers' association warns that if the handover is treated as routine administration, coal may not move on the first day [S16]. For this group a material slice of revenue is exported — US$186.9m directly to third-party buyers and US$477.5m through the affiliate marketing arm, with Singapore the largest destination at US$545.8m [S13, F42, F25, F43]. But the rule changes the counterparty and the documentation, not the price: no coal-specific fee is disclosed in any archived source, so we carry execution risk rather than a price or volume assumption [S15, S16].

Competitive position is unattractive in the medium term. Buyer power is high because steel mills blend; rivalry is intense where supply discipline is a policy choice; supplier power is rising for diesel-linked equipment and fuel; substitutes run through steelmaking technology over decades; and new entrants are contained by licensing rather than geology [S7, S12]. The one force in the group's favour is domestic industrial demand from the park, and that is a plan rather than a position today [S7].

The external drivers are the commodity decks, the rupiah and the group's funding cost: the macro deck carries the rupiah at **Rp17,570/USD** in the current year against a reviewed spot of **Rp18,039/USD**, which matters twice for a dollar reporter listed in Jakarta, in translation and in the rupiah cost base [S0].

The September print is the largest forecast revision. Revenue for the nine months was **US$1,901.5m**, gross profit **US$776.3m** at a margin of **40.8%** against the **34.0%** of the audited year, parent profit **US$516.6m** against **US$447.7m** for the whole of FY2025, and the effective tax rate **16.8%** on the metal segment's facility [S18, F46, F47, F48, F49, F50]. We set FY2026E revenue at **US$2,803.9m** — the nine months plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's own run rate, which is why growth is **49.6%** — then hold it broadly flat as the smelter runs a full year and the coal deck reverts [S18, S0]. EBITDA is **US$1,251.4m** at a margin of **44.6%** [S0, S18]. For FY2025A the company prints its own operational EBITDA of **US$799.0m** at a **43.0%** margin [S3, F6, F10]; our derived figure is **US$767.0m** at **40.9%**, a definitional gap that does not reach the valuation [S3, S18].

The calibration gate re-prices FY2026E at the FY2025A benchmark and volume and compares the model's EBITDA margin of **44.6%** with the actual **40.9%**; the gap is the aluminium mix, whose revenue and cost carry a different margin from coal and services, not a cost assumption [S18, F46, F47, F61].

Cash is where the prior draft was wrong. The filing prints cash and cash equivalents of **US$1,044.1m** at the audited year-end and **US$1,405.9m** for the prior year, not the pack's wider line that folds the current portion of other investments in; we restated both years, so net debt and leverage start from the cash the company reports [S13, F72, F73]. The forecast carries the September debt position of **US$1,827.6m** — bank loans plus lease liabilities — against year-end cash of **US$1,567.8m**, giving net debt of **US$259.8m** and net debt to EBITDA of **0.21** [S18, F54, F55, F56, F51]. That is below the September position because the fourth quarter is the strongest cash quarter [S18, F58, F69].

The funding reversal is real: operating cash flow of **US$390.7m** did not cover the **US$447.5m** paid to shareholders, **US$485.6m** of new bank loans was drawn, and the group moved from net cash to net debt [S18, F58, F69, F70]. We carry the payout at **60%**, above the four-year mean and below the FY2025 near-total distribution: the company has demonstrated it will pay out roughly the absolute amount we forecast, but a repeat at the FY2025 ratio on a higher profit would be a further step up in borrowing, which is not the most likely path [S6, F8, S18]. At the four-year mean payout the distribution is smaller and the total return lower, so the above-mean payout is not what carries the call [S6, F18]. Capital expenditure falls to **8.2%** of revenue as the smelter completes commissioning, from the **US$662.0m** the subsidiary spent in FY2025, and the nine-month cash flow shows **US$131.1m** of fixed-asset payments [S14, F38, F39, F71, S18].

Working capital has flipped from a source of cash to a use. The model holds operating working capital at **24.6%** of revenue because the aluminium business ties up inventory and receivables; inventories were **US$509.8m** at September against a fraction of that at the year start [S18, F59, S0]. On earnings quality, the depreciation charge is now the audited one, restated from the notes at **US$237.5m** with mining-property amortisation of **US$17.9m**, so EBITDA is not flattered by the pack's fraction [S13, F12, F14]. The flags that remain are the payout, which exceeded operating cash flow, and related parties: **US$883.6m** of nine-month revenue was still billed to related parties, below FY2025's **74.1%** because the third-party aluminium book grew [S18, F60, F26].

The method set is the house standard for a holding company: the group is worth what it owns — a listed subsidiary, a contractor, joint ventures, a securities book and parent net cash — and no single consolidated cash flow describes that mix. Two parts are marks rather than prices: the contractor is unlisted, and the joint ventures and securities are at fair value or book [S13, S18].

The primary sums the parts. The subsidiary is at its traded price on the audited ownership of **85%** [S13, F33, S0]. The contractor is at its September segment net assets of **US$1,089.9m** less **US$233.1m**; that is an unaudited interim mark, not the audited FY2025 figure of **US$897.1m** less **US$251.9m**, and it is intended because it is the latest balance sheet and captures the working capital the smelter haulage now requires [S18, F63, F64, F27, F28]. The joint ventures are at **US$740.2m** and the parent's FVOCI securities at **US$728.3m**, both fair-value or book marks [S18, F52, F53]. The parent's other investments are completed by the **US$105.0m** FVTPL sleeve: the group totals **US$942.9m**, the subsidiary's own statements carry only **US$26.3m** current and **US$83.3m** non-current, and the residual is a real part and not a double count [S18, F74, F75, F76, S19, F77, F78]. Against the parts sit the parent cost base capitalised at the house card's multiple, **US$61.7m** of G&A, and the holdco net cash computed from the consolidated and subsidiary statements [S13, F44, S18, S19, F51, F54, F55, F56, F65, F66, F67].

The one dated capital action sits at the parent and not in the parts. The 17 April 2026 AGMS authorised a buyback of up to 5.0 trillion rupiah for 12.0 months from 18 April 2026, and execution began on 20 October 2026 [S20, S21, F79, F80]. At the tape that ceiling is less than a tenth of the shares; because it is below the pre-discount net asset value per share but above the discounted SOTP value, it transfers value to the shares that remain and argues that the discount is wide rather than that it is closing. No repurchased volume is disclosed, so the base case keeps the share count and the 30% discount and carries the window as the dated catalyst the thesis was missing [S18, S20, S21].

The cost of capital is reported for completeness; the primary leg does not discount a cash flow. The risk-free rate is **4.86%**, the mature equity risk premium **4.23%** and the country premium **2.46%**; with an unlevered beta of **0.90** and modelled gearing the levered beta is **1.25**, the cost of equity **13.22%** and WACC **10.6%** [S0, S13].

Neither multiple cross-check carries weight, and the reason is the same for both: their history spans the AADI separation. The own-history P/E is a peak-earnings artefact over the super-cycle, applied to post-separation earnings [S0, S13]. The P/BV leg would apply the group's four-year average to the September 2026 parent-attributable equity of **US$5,031.4m**, but the first of those years is struck on the pre-separation entity, whose pack revenue is more than three times the FY2023A figure because it still owned the thermal business later separated into AADI [S0, S13, F57]. That outlier lifts the average; restricted to the post-separation years the multiple is lower, and the target stays in the hold range once the distribution is counted, so the rating is a hold either way [S0, S18]. A weighted leg on the full history would have printed an add — the artefact the audit caught — and embedded a discount far narrower than the one we underwrite [S0, S13, S18].

The parts are marks, and two can move against us. The FVOCI securities and the joint ventures are fair value and book, not floors: the securities sleeve rose to **US$728.3m** in nine months, and a one-fifth markdown alone would remove a low-single-digit percentage of the SOTP value, while a similar markdown of the joint ventures would remove more [S18, F52, F53]. Neither is shocked in the scenario column because the engine cannot move a static mark [S0]. The limitation cuts both ways: the subsidiary's tape already carries the smelter ramp, and its re-rating is not in the bull column either [S14, F33, F37].

Against the SOTP net asset value, the price of **Rp2,310** implies a discount of **23%**, and we underwrite **30%**, so the SOTP prints below the tape and the return on the target is a hold [S0, S18]. The implied value reverses the same arithmetic: at our discount the parts would justify the price only if the marks were higher, so the price is a statement about the discount and the book, not the coal price [S0].

The largest downside is governance and the marks, not the coal price. A markdown of the securities and joint-venture books is medium likelihood and high impact because they are fair-value and book marks with no observable exit: a one-fifth fall in the securities sleeve alone is a low-single-digit percentage of the parts, and the joint ventures carry the same risk with less transparency [S18, F52, F53]. The ADMR mark is the second: it is more than half of the gross parts and the house's view of it is a reduce well below the tape, so its re-rating is the largest swing factor either way [S0, F33].

Regulatory risk is dated and executional. The state export channel starts on 1 January 2027; a botched permit handover would stop shipments for a quarter or more, and the association has warned of exactly that [S15, S16]. Impact is high on the subsidiary's cash and medium on the parent, because the parent is a look-through holder. Commodity risk is medium: the coal deck already assumes reversion and the aluminium deck a long-run marker, so a further fall is a second-order move against the marks [S0, S7]. Funding and liquidity risk is medium: the group is now a net borrower after a distribution that exceeded operating cash flow, and it still funds an industrial programme and a payout from the same cash [S18, F58, F69, F70]. Related-party risk is structural and already reflected in the contractor mark rather than the margin [S18, F60, F26]. FX matters for translation and for the rupiah cost base [S0].

The scenario set is discount-only: bear and bull move the holdco discount by the same amount in opposite directions and nothing else, because the engine cannot shock the static marks [S0]. The bear widens the discount to the top of the house band as the met-coal tape rolls over and the export handover snags; the bull narrows it to the floor as the smelter ramps, the coal complex holds above the deck and the handover arrives clean, with no re-rating of the subsidiary or the securities book taken in either case [S15, S16, F37]. The probabilities are one quarter, one half and one quarter [S0].

The house-view stress is not in the table and is the one to watch. Re-marking the subsidiary to the house's own value lowers the blend to just above the bear's **Rp1,777** and takes the total return to about minus eight per cent once the Rp269 distribution is counted, a stronger sell case than a hold; that is why the subsidiary's own coverage is a reduce while this parent is a hold — the difference is the mark, not the business [S0, F33]. The nearest dated catalyst is now the buyback window: a ceiling priced below the pre-discount net asset value supports a narrower discount from the inside, but it cannot crystallise the unlisted marks, and disclosed execution is what would move us [S20, S21]. The signposts are that execution, a subsidiary re-rating, a distribution policy reset, and a clean or botched export handover [S6, S15, S16].

The parent is controlled by the founding family's vehicle; the insider field of **69.0%** and free float of **26.6%** leave a small residual that we read as treasury and other non-float holdings [S0, S8]. No pledge is disclosed and the treasury shares were cancelled, so there is no overhang [S8, S13]. The listed subsidiary is separately traded with its own minority, so related-party flows run at both levels: revenue of **US$1,387.9m** in FY2025 and **US$883.6m** in the nine months is the number to monitor [S13, S18, F16, F60].

The dividend record is the clearest governance signal: a payout of **100.0%** in FY2025 and a forecast above the four-year mean, with the policy conditioned on financial capability rather than a fixed ratio, and the FY2025 distribution approved at the AGM [S6, F8]. The auditor's opinion on the audited accounts is unqualified in the archived report, and no restatement or auditor change is disclosed [S13]. The board is controlled through the family vehicle and the subsidiary's board overlaps with the parent's, which is normal for this structure and is why we capitalise the parent cost base and discount the parts rather than trust a consolidated margin [S13, S7].

ESG exposure is dominated by coal and the industrial build. The met-coal product faces end-market decarbonisation over decades, the smelter is a large power consumer whose hydro backing is its licence to operate, and reclamation and closure obligations sit inside the mining permits and are provided for in the accounts [S13, S7]. Related-party transfers and cross-guarantees at either level widen the warranted discount [S13, F16].

The dated catalysts are the buyback window that runs to 17 April 2027 and any disclosed execution within it, the state export channel on 1 January 2027, the FY2026 results and declared distribution, the AGM decision on capital actions, and the North Kalimantan hydro and industrial park funding decision [S20, S21, S15, S16, S6, S7]. The KPIs we monitor are the subsidiary's coal sales and the smelter's ramp, the aluminium revenue and margin, the parent's cash and gross debt, the declared payout against our forecast, and related-party revenue [S18, S14, F37, F61, F58, F60]. A second period of distribution above operating cash flow would signal that the funding reversal is structural and would move us toward the bear [S18, F58, F69].

bear.narrative: Discount-only: the holdco discount widens to the top of the house band as the met-coal tape rolls over and the new state export channel snags the subsidiary's shipments at the 1 January 2027 handover, with the securities and joint-venture marks carried at their September values and no credit taken for a markdown because no sourced price exists for the unlisted book [S15, S16, S13, F25, F42].

bull.narrative: Discount-only: the discount narrows to the floor of the house band as the ADMR smelter ramps, the coal complex holds above the deck's reversion path, and the 1 January 2027 handover arrives clean and fee-free so the affiliate marketing margin returns to the producer; the ADMR mark is held at its traded price and no re-rating of it or of the securities book is taken, so the bull sizes the discount only [S15, S16, S13, F37].

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the nine-month actual, not on the pre-results forecast. The Q3-2026 LK reports revenue of 1,901.5 for the nine months to September against 1,874.0 for the whole of FY2025, so the current year is already above the last full year before the fourth quarter; carrying a fourth quarter at the third quarter's own run rate gives 2,803.8 for FY2026E, about +50%, and that is the growth we carry rather than the slightly higher figure a full-year extrapolation would give. The step is not a coal-price call: it is the aluminium smelter's first sales, 522.4 in the nine months and all to third parties, on top of a mining book of 725.1 external and a services book of 623.0 (S18, F46, F61, F46). FY2027E is held broadly flat because the smelter runs a full year at the same capacity while the coal book is carried at the reviewed deck's reversion, and the outer years ease as the deck settles. The primary SOTP has no revenue line, so this path reaches the target only through the forward distribution and the earnings cross-check, not through the parts (S18, S0, S13).

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Held at the last reported nine-month ratio, which is the most recent actual and reflects the changed mix: gross profit of 776.3 on revenue of 1,901.5 is 40.83%, against the 33.99% of the FY2025 audited year, because the aluminium sales (522.4 of revenue, 337.8 of cost) carry a different margin from the coal and services books. No disclosed contract or input-cost change justifies a further move, so the ratio is held flat rather than faded, and the aluminium ramp's working-capital drag is carried in the cash flow rather than in the margin. [S18, F46, F47, F61]

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the last reported nine-month ratio: operating expenses of 94.95 on revenue of 1,901.5 is 4.99%, against 5.72% for the FY2025 audited year, because the fixed overhead is spread over the larger aluminium-inclusive revenue base. No step-up is disclosed for the industrial build, so the current ratio is carried flat. [S18, F46]

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the segment note, which prints total depreciation and amortisation of 185.998 for the nine months to September on revenue of 1,901.5; annualised that is about 248 on the larger revenue base, 8.8%, so the ratio is set there rather than at the 12.68% the smaller FY2025 revenue base implied. The data pack's D&A line remains a fraction of the real charge. [S18, F62, F46]

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Anchored on what the nine-month cash flow actually shows and on the company's own guidance. The LK reports payments for fixed-asset additions of 131.1 in the nine months to September; the metallurgical-coal subsidiary that carries the smelter guides FY2026 group capex to a range beginning at 220 and ending at 240, from 662 in FY2025 (S14), so a fourth quarter of roughly 100 gives about 231 for the year, or 8.2% of the 2,830 revenue we forecast, not the 17.7% the old, smaller revenue base implied. The intensity then eases toward a sustaining level as the smelter completes commissioning and ramps to full capacity during 2026. [S18, S14, F62]

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Moved to the last reported balance: operating working capital was 467.9 at 30-Sep-2026 on revenue of 1,901.5 for the nine months, 24.6% of revenue, against negative 173.7 at the audited year-end. The swing is the aluminium business: inventories rose to 509.8 from 116.0 and receivables to 415.6 as the smelter ramps, so working capital is now a use of cash rather than a source, and holding the old negative ratio would credit the forecast with a release that the accounts contradict. [S18, F59, S0]

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Held at the last reported effective rate: income tax of 122.3 on pre-tax profit of 728.9 in the nine months to September is 16.78%, below the FY2025 audited 20.0% because the metal-processing segment reports no tax charge in the same note, consistent with the smelter's tax facility. The current rate is the most recent actual and is carried flat. [S18, F49, F50]

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Raised to the rate the nine-month accounts imply: finance costs of 61.5, of which lease interest alone is 51.9 (note 18), against debt that averaged roughly 1,300 over the period, is about 6%; the old 2.04% was struck on the pre-lease, pre-smelter debt stack and no longer describes the company. [S18]

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025A interest income 97.5 on opening cash 2,033.6. [S13, S0]

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the observed balance sheet, not zero. The September-2026 position shows gross debt of 1,827.6 (bank loans 1,091.6 plus lease liabilities 736.0) against the 821.3 audited at 31-Dec-2025, a rise of 1,006.3 in nine months, so FY2026E carries that 1,006.3 and its year-end debt reproduces the September balance the sum-of-the-parts and the equity bridge both use (S18, F54, F55, F56). The rise is not coal-seasonal: it is the smelter's project finance and the new building-and-equipment leases the company describes in its own commentary (S17). Thereafter borrowing is sized to the residual funding gap after the guided capex taper, a small annual figure rather than peak-programme drawdowns, because the smelter's construction spend is winding down. (S18, S13, S14, S17)

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Raised to the last reported ratio: non-controlling interests of 90.1 on profit for the period of 606.7 in the nine months to September is 14.85%, against 8.60% for FY2025A, because a larger share of profit now comes from the metal-processing segment that is 56% owned. The minority share is the one that the smelter's ramp raises, so holding the old ratio would overstate the parent's claim on group profit. [S18, F48, F49]

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The payout now steps to 60% in FY2026E, above the four-year mean of 48.7% (69.63%, 40.00%, 48.74% and 36.23% in 2021-2024), rather than staying at the FY2025 outlier. The September accounts show why a step is needed but why 99.96% cannot repeat: the group paid 447.5 of dividends in the nine months — the FY2025 near-total distribution — while operating cash flow was only 390.7, so the payout was funded by drawing bank loans of 485.6, and the consolidated balance sheet moved from net cash at the audited year-end to net debt of 662.6 (S18, F58). A repeat at 99.96% of a materially higher profit would be a further step up in borrowing, which is not the most likely path; the capex taper (8.2% of revenue against 17.7% implied for FY2025) and the subsidiary's upstreamed cash (admr_dividend_paid 120.0 in the nine months) are what support a payout still above the four-year mean. The company's own distribution table shows payouts of 69.63% (2021), 40.00% (2022), 48.74% (2023), 36.23% (2024) and 99.96% (2025), and its policy conditions the dividend on financial capability and capital adequacy, not on a fixed ratio (S6, F8). At 60% the absolute distribution is about the same as the one just paid, so the forecast holds the cash distribution rather than assuming it grows with profit; the dividend is a forecast, not a declared amount. The subsidiary is marked at its own traded price, so its dividends and payout policy are already inside the stake mark and are not added a second time.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No placement is disclosed since the 2025 treasury-share cancellation, but a buyback is: the 17-Apr-2026 AGMS approved a repurchase of up to Rp5 trn for the 12 months from 18 April 2026, and execution began on 20 October 2026 with treasury shares nil at the 30-Sep-2026 balance-sheet date, so the action is genuinely post-date [S18, S20, S21, F79, F80]. No repurchased volume is disclosed to date, so the base case carries no share-count change. Full execution at the tape would retire less than a tenth of the shares and, because the ceiling price is below the pre-discount net asset value per share, would lift the value of the shares that remain by a low single-digit percentage of net asset value; that upper bound is disclosed in section 4 as a capital action rather than modelled into the base case.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for a USD reporter, held inside the house cap of 2.5%; it is not used by the primary sum-of-the-parts method, only by the terminal value of any cash-flow leg. [S0]

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 30%, the midpoint of the house persistent band: VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT holds that holdco discounts of 20-40% persist by default and that the discount is the base rate, not the opportunity. The name has no usable five-year discount history (ADMR listed in 2022 and the parent's structure changed with the thermal spin in Dec-2024). The one dated holdco capital action is the buyback approved at the 17-Apr-2026 AGMS (up to Rp5 trn over the 12 months from 18 April 2026, execution from 20 October 2026) [S20, S21, F79, F80]; it is a discretionary repurchase of less than a tenth of the shares, priced below the pre-discount net asset value per share but above the discounted SOTP value, so it supports the view that the discount is wide without crystallising an upstream mark. It is carried as a catalyst that could narrow the discount, not as one that already has, so the base case holds 30%, the middle of the band. [S4, S13]
